tna-defe24-1948-rendlesham-1980.precision_label: Named site location from OpenStreetMap, not an event fix
tna-defe24-1948-rendlesham-1980.precision_note: The official record names the back gate at RAF Woodbridge and an area of Rendlesham Forest, but does not print coordinates. Official gazetteer coordinates were not retrieved in the source pack. The shaded outlines are the OpenStreetMap features for Rendlesham Forest and for MOD Woodbridge (Rock Barracks). No OpenStreetMap feature named “back gate” or “RAF Woodbridge” was found. An OSM tourism viewpoint named “Rendlesham East Gate” exists in the forest area; it is not used here as the official back-gate location, because the official record does not use that name and does not give coordinates.
tna-defe24-1948-rendlesham-1980.time_as_printed: Approximately 0300L on 27 Dec 80; no clock time given for 29 Dec 80; paragraph 3 begins “Later in the night.”
tna-defe24-1948-rendlesham-1980.date_as_printed: Memorandum date: 13 Jan 81. First reported observation: “Early in the morning of 27 Dec 80 (approximately 0300L).” Radiation check: “The following night (29 Dec 80).”
tna-defe24-1948-rendlesham-1980.official_status: Officially confirmed (that the report exists): The UK National Archives holds the Ministry of Defence file and presents the Halt memorandum as the “single sheet report” that is “the only record of the event itself” in its holdings. A 16 October 2001 House of Lords written answer stated that this was the only USAF material held by the MoD on the incident, that MoD records from the same period “document no evidence of unusual radar returns,” and that there was “no indication from the papers held on file that MoD raised any further questions with Lieutenant Colonel Halt following receipt of his memorandum in 1981.” The National Archives collection page says a note in response to a Parliamentary Question “confirmed that there was nothing of defence interest in the alleged sighting.”
tna-defe24-1948-rendlesham-1980.place_label: Back gate at RAF Woodbridge, and Rendlesham Forest, Suffolk
tna-defe24-1948-rendlesham-1980.place_as_written: “unusual lights outside the back gate at RAF Woodbridge”; a “strange glowing object in the forest”; later “near the back gate”; then “the area” where depressions were found. The UK National Archives collection page places the events at “a Royal Air Force (RAF) base in Suffolk,” names RAF Woodbridge, and says servicemen “investigated an area of Rendlesham Forest on two separate nights.”
tna-defe24-1948-rendlesham-1980.incident_date_source: First reported observation in the Halt memorandum: Early in the morning of 27 Dec 80 (approximately 0300L). Later nights are not used for the period-map date.

street_view.note: Camera is framed at the midpoint between the OpenStreetMap centroids of Rendlesham Forest (52.0865885, 1.4093625) and MOD Woodbridge (52.0854659, 1.3894825), so both named-site outlines can be seen. This midpoint is a view-framing aid only. It is not an event fix and is not the back gate.
